stage1.impression: It reads as a CG speaker showroom, not a photograph of a bar at night. The frame is a fir-lined niche with one speaker and half of another, lit evenly, over a flat black floor and a dead dark slab on the left, with no lamps, no people-traces and no props. At 1:1 the panelling is a clean repeating veneer with no checks or nail holes, the horn has a hard white cut-out halo, and the white batt block is a flat near-clipped rectangle. A design magazine would not publish this as a specific place: it shows a generic display niche, not Planet EARF.

blocking_9: The frame shows none of what the card says it is for: no tub chairs in the foreground, no 200 mm step, no altar, no Core lamps on small tables, no props. The room has to be reframed and checked to be complete before lighting can be judged.
The pair is cut in half by the right edge [1030,140,1200,800]. Both Tropos have to be whole, or the composition has to commit to one.
The fir wall is lit evenly from top to bottom (profile 68-78 across six of eight bins) and is brighter than the speaker's body. It needs pools of light and falloff, not a flat wash.
The floor [0,690,1000,800] is a featureless field (lum_range 9.9). It needs texture, sheen or a reflection of the pools.
No sign of life is visible in frame (glass, record, coat).
The horn's white outline halo (edge step -161 over 11 px at [335,250,360,260]) reads as a cut-out or composite.
The white batt block [355,320,520,400] sits at lum_median 247, flat and nearly clipped, and reads as a white box.

defects.what: Second speaker cropped in half at the right edge; a lower slab of something beige at [1060,670,1200,800] is unreadable
Horn rim has a bright white uniform outline, like a cut-out matte or emission edge; the black horn's reflections are glossy, plastic-looking smears
Batt block flat white at 247, no texture or gradation, reads as a lightbox
Plinth top edge glows white, clip_pct 2.0, a hard light line like LED signage
Floor flat dark brown, lum_range 9.9, no texture, sheen or light pools; speaker and plinth do not ground on it convincingly
Dead dark slab of wall, lum_median 21, range 9.4, no material read
Fir panelling reads as uniform, too-clean red walnut veneer (r 104 g 65 b 45) with no checks, nail holes or board variation; lit evenly with no pools
Dark panel behind the speaker is a flat featureless rectangle that reads as a placeholder
No props, lamps, chairs or haze visible although the card lists them; the scene looks incomplete or the camera misses them

changes.problem: The camera frames a bare niche, not the card's hero view from behind the tub chairs with the pair, the altar and the Core lamps.

evidence.measured: No chairs, step, altar, lamps or props are visible; the right speaker is cut at x 1030-1200; the left 120 px is a dead slab (median 21)

change.to: pull back about 1.5-2 m (x ~11.5) and centre on the zone (y ~3.0) at seated eye height (z ~1.1), target [16.5, 3.0, 1.0], 28-30 mm, so the backs of two tub chairs frame the lower foreground, the step reads, and both Tropos and the altar sit whole between the thirds; then verify that the props and lamps the card lists actually render

changes.expected: A specific room: foreground velvet chairs, a mid-ground step and altar with the pair, and lamps on small tables as pools of light.

changes.problem: The fir wall gets a flat wash brighter than the speaker's body, and the niche strip burns a white line along the plinth top.

evidence.measured: lum_median 72, y-profile 68-78 flat over 6 of 8 bins; plinth top [335,580,560,610] clip_pct 2.0

change.setting: the lit niche's strip (emission) and the altar spots
change.from: strip 6.0; altar 2 x spot 70 W, cone 14 deg
change.to: strip 2.0; altar spots kept at 70 W but aimed at the speakers' faces and the plinth tops so the wall above gets only spill

changes.expected: The wall falls off from a pool around the speakers into dark at the top, and the plinth edge reads as wood, not as a light strip.

changes.problem: The white batt block is nearly clipped and flat, so the speaker reads as a white box instead of light passing through tinted acrylic.

change.setting: on each Ember speaker 4 x area lamps
change.to: 0.10 W/m2, 2700 K, moved off-axis (about 45 deg above and to the side) so the batts get a gradient

changes.expected: The batts show texture and gradation under the smoked acrylic, peaking around 200, not 247.

changes.problem: The horn's rim carries a uniform white halo that reads as a cut-out outline.

evidence.measured: edge step -161.4, width 11 px; a continuous white line all round the horn [340,195,530,310]

change.setting: Ember area lamps' position (with c3) plus render clamp
change.from: area lamps near the camera axis; clamp 10
change.to: area lamps off-axis as in c3 so the rim catches a highlight on one side only; clamp 4

changes.expected: The rim reads as a polished edge with a broken, one-sided highlight, not an outline.

changes.problem: The floor is a featureless dark field and grounds nothing.

change.to: honed concrete with soft sheen (roughness about 0.35), visible aggregate and faint staining, so the altar pools and plinths reflect softly

changes.expected: Soft reflections of the pools and plinths, and visible texture in the floor.

changes.problem: The room's own practicals are effectively off, so there are no pools of light and no cosiness.

evidence.measured: dead slab lum_median 21, range 9.4; Orb at 0.05 W, glow 0.0008 per the card

change.setting: each Orb (Core lamp) wattage and liner glow
change.to: 0.8 W, glow 0.015, so each table lamp throws a warm pool on its table and on the nearby chair arm

changes.expected: Two or three warm pools in the foreground and mid-ground with dark between them; the lamps' liners are bright but not blown.

changes.problem: Nothing in frame says someone is here.

evidence.measured: No glass, record, sleeve or coat visible

change.from: listed on the card but out of frame
change.to: place in frame: a sleeve leaning on the near plinth, a rocks glass and a record on the small table under an Orb, and the coat over the nearest tub chair's arm

changes.expected: A lived-in foreground that catches small highlights from the pools.

changes.problem: The panelling reads as clean, red, repeating veneer, not old Douglas fir, and pushes the room toward orange-red.

evidence.measured: r 97 g 59 b 41; uniform grain with no checks, nail holes or board-to-board tone variation

change.setting: the fir's finish / stain, and haze
change.to: a honey-tan, less saturated stain with per-board tone variation, checks and darker end grain; haze 0.007 so the altar spot cones just read

changes.expected: The wood reads as real fir boards, and the frame's warmth comes from the 2400-2700 K light rather than red paint.

out_of_scope.request: Make the horn's black resin read less like glossy plastic (its reflections are smeary)
out_of_scope.why: The horn's material and shape are EARF's fixed product.

out_of_scope.request: Give the speaker colour so it is the frame's one saturated hue
out_of_scope.why: The Smoke configuration is a fixed product tint; in Smoke the hero has to be carried by light and composition, not colour.

out_of_scope.request: Replace the flat dark panel behind the speaker with something with material
out_of_scope.why: The niche's design and materials are fixed by the card. If the panel is meant to be blackened steel, its finish (patina, uneven sheen) may be changed under 'materials' finish', but its presence may not.
